newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan calls for Afghan military restraint.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan calls for Afghan military restraint.

text.p: Pakistan has called for military restraint in neighbouring Afghanistan and for the formation of a broad-based government there, the official APP news agency said on Friday.

APP quoted Foreign Ministry secretary Najmuddin Sheikh as saying in a statement to Pakistani reporters that Islamabad "believes that the interest of the people of Afghanistan would be best served if there were no further military action against those forces which were willing to enter into political negotiations to form a broad-based government".
He said Pakistan believed "such a broad-based government providing representation to all areas of Afghanistan would bring much-needed stability".
APP also quoted Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto as saying in New York that Islamabad would send an envoy to neighbouring countries to coordinate action to bring peace to Afghanistan.
Pakistan denies charges from Afghanistan's ousted government of president Burhanuddin Rabbani that Islamabad gave military help to the Taleban.
The hardline Islamic movement has taken control of about three quarters of the war-torn country and captured the capital Kabul a week ago.

APP quoted Sheikh as saying that the 52-nation Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC) intended to send a peace mission to Afghanistan. OIC secretary-general Hamid al-Gabid met Bhutto on Thursday in New York.
